To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
county level official media in China are not independent from the central and provincial government and are thus unable to serve as effective public space.

1) the county level media are more autonomous from the state than the national media, but they are still under tight control; 2) the county level journalists have a stronger sense of professionalism than their national counterparts, but they are not as independent; 3) the county level public spaces are more open than national ones, but they are less effective in terms of public participation; and 4) the county level newspapers are less effective in serving as an arena for public deliberation, and
county level official media outlets are not effective channels for the public to express their views and opinions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether media outlets at the local level can be effective public spaces for participation and representation, and the findings suggest that this is not necessarily the case.
the role of the local press and its potential for promoting public space in China.
the role of public space in the Chinese media system, with a focus on the role of the media in the political process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
county level media outlets are not effective channels of participation and representation, although the situation is improving.
, although the county level media outlets are less controlled and enjoy a higher degree of autonomy than the national media, they are far from constituting a public sphere in the Western sense.
county level media are still not effective channels for public debate and representation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Chinese public space is not a space for public participation.
the media system in China is still a top-down, state-dominated, one-party-controlled system, and that there is little space for public participation and representation.
the Chinese media are still far from being effective channels for participation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the state is not the only actor that matters in shaping media outlets in China.
the media system at the county level is a product of the state’s political control, rather than an arena for public participation.
the Chinese media system is a highly complex network, and the media at the county level should not be seen as a panacea for China's public sphere.
